examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'водник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'matchmakers' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой не сводники.
examples.trans: You and I are not matchmakers after all.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть сводник.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always matchmakers.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Нет, конечно, мы вмешиваться не будем.
examples.trans: No, of course, we will not interfere.

examples.text: Конечно, пойдём скорее садиться в машину.
examples.trans: Of course, let us go get in the car quickly.

examples.text: Конечно, со мной всё совершенно нормально.
examples.trans: Of course, everything is completely normal with me.

вмешиваться.gloss: to interfere, to meddle, to intervene

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to interfere, to meddle, to intervene', paired with 'вмешаться'.

examples.text: Нет, конечно, мы вмешиваться не будем.
examples.trans: No, of course, we will not interfere.

examples.text: А вы не вмешивайтесь.
examples.trans: And you, stay out of it.

examples.text: Подарки надо ценить! А вы не вмешивайтесь.
examples.trans: You must appreciate gifts! And you, stay out of it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let (them)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

examples.text: Да, пусть решают всё сами.
examples.trans: Yes, let them decide everything themselves.

examples.text: Пусть он немного посидит вместе с нами.
examples.trans: Let him sit with us for a little while.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Лёва, тут дело очень тонкое.
examples.trans: You understand, Lyova, this is a very delicate matter.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'ourselves', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он высокий и с красивыми усами.
examples.trans: He is tall and has a handsome mustache.

examples.text: Может, самое время Денису подойти к ней?
examples.trans: Maybe this is the right time for Denis to approach her?

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С тобой сегодня вечером так весело!
examples.trans: It is so much fun with you tonight!

examples.text: С ним за столом всегда так весело!
examples.trans: It is always so cheerful at the table with him!

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.en: to know one's stuff, be well versed in
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'бираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'разобраться'.

examples.text: Я же строитель, я разбираюсь.
examples.trans: I'm a builder, I know my stuff.

examples.text: О, смотри, у тебя вон щели! Я же строитель, я разбираюсь.
examples.trans: Oh, look, you have gaps over there! I'm a builder, I know my stuff.

examples.text: Твоя мама отлично разбирается в рыбе?
examples.trans: Does your mother understand fish well?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, Лёва, что там случилось?
examples.trans: Yes, Lyova, what happened over there?

examples.text: Да, это время нам отлично подходит.
examples.trans: Yes, that time suits us very well.

examples.text: Вообще непонятно, чего от него ждать.
examples.trans: There is no telling what to expect from him.

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'solve', paired with 'решить'.

examples.text: Да, пусть решают всё сами.
examples.trans: Yes, let them decide everything themselves.

examples.text: Сами решайте, что делать.
examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Мы вместе решаем все вопросы.
examples.trans: We decide all matters together.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лена, у меня всё в порядке!
examples.trans: Lena, everything is fine with me!

examples.text: Я потом тебе всё подробно расскажу.
examples.trans: I will tell you everything in detail later.

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.
